I want to introduce “a graphical framework in which we can analyze the Markov properties from a purely set theoretic perspective which is independent of probability theory,”

Motivation: I was trying to provide a common foundation connecting graphical models in statistics, random fields, and percolation on lattices. Along the way, I found that most of the materials I read assumed finite vertex sets. However, I want to understand better what drives the equivalence of the Markov properties, so that we can talk about theorems with more flexibility. I then found this paper, which, in Section 4, takes a purely set-theoretic approach to independence and graphical Markov properties, separately from its treatment of measure-theoretic conditional independence in probabilistic models.

If this PR meets the requirements and is in the right direction, I plan to finish proving the equivalence of the pairwise, local, and global Markov properties for ternary relations under suitable intersection assumptions. In the long term, I plan to connect conditional independence in probability with graphical models, including DAGs.
